title: Aurora Borealis Shader
prompt: Create an interactive Aurora Borealis (Northern Lights) visualization using Three.js with custom shaders. ## Scene Setup - Black background (color: 0x000005) representing a night sky. - PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 8), looking at origin, FOV 60. - A large ground plane (100x100) at y=-2 with dark terrain color (0x0a0a15), representing snowy tundra. - Starfield: Create 500 small white points (BufferGeometry with random positions) scattered in a hemisphere above y=0, radius 50. Use PointsMaterial with size 0.1. ## Aurora Curtain (Main Feature) - Create a custom ShaderMaterial applied to a PlaneGeometry(20, 8, 128, 64) positioned at (0, 4, -5). - The vertex shader should displace vertices using layered sine waves based on time uniform `uTime`, creating a flowing curtain effect. Displacement formula: `pos.x += sin(pos.y * 2.0 + uTime * 0.5) * 0.5; pos.z += cos(pos.x * 1.5 + uTime * 0.3) * 0.3;` - The fragment shader should mix colors between green (0.1, 0.8, 0.3), cyan (0.1, 0.6, 0.9), and purple (0.5, 0.1, 0.8) based on UV coordinates and time. Use `uIntensity` uniform (0.0-1.0) to control brightness. Use `uColorMode` uniform (int: 0=green-cyan, 1=red-orange, 2=purple-blue) to select color palettes. - The material should be transparent with blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, side: THREE.DoubleSide, depthWrite: false. ## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__) Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__: - `animating` (boolean): Whether the animation loop is running. Start as true. - `elapsedTime` (number): The accumulated time passed to shaders (seconds). Starts at 0. - `intensity` (number): Aurora brightness from 0.0 to 1.0. Default 0.7. - `colorMode` (number): 0, 1, or 2. Default 0. - `cameraY` (number): Current camera Y position. Default 2. - `cameraZ` (number): Current camera Z position. Default 8. - `curtainVisible` (boolean): Whether the aurora curtain mesh is visible. Default true. - `starCount` (number): Number of stars. Should be 500. - `groundVisible` (boolean): Whether ground plane is visible. Default true. - `speedMultiplier` (number): Animation speed multiplier. Default 1.0. Range 0.25 to 4.0. - `layerCount` (number): Number of aurora curtain layers. Default 1. Can be 1, 2, or 3. ## UI Controls (DOM) - A HUD panel (id='hud') positioned top-left with semi-transparent dark background, containing: - A label showing current intensity as percentage: `Intensity: 70%` - A label showing color mode name: `Color: Green-Cyan` - A label showing speed: `Speed: 1.0x` - A label showing layers: `Layers: 1` - Buttons: - `` - Toggles animation on/off. - `` - Resets all values to defaults. ## Keyboard Interactions - ArrowUp: Increase intensity by 0.1 (max 1.0) - ArrowDown: Decrease intensity by 0.1 (min 0.0) - 'C' or 'c': Cycle color mode (0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0) - 'G' or 'g': Toggle ground visibility - 'H' or 'h': Toggle aurora curtain visibility - '+' or '=': Increase speed multiplier by 0.25 (max 4.0) - '-' or '_': Decrease speed multiplier by 0.25 (min 0.25) - 'L' or 'l': Cycle layer count (1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1). When adding layers, clone the aurora mesh with slight z-offset (+1.5 per layer) and slight color variation. - 'W' or 'w': Move camera forward (decrease cameraZ by 0.5, min 2) - 'S' or 's': Move camera backward (increase cameraZ by 0.5, max 15) ## Animation Loop - Each frame, if animating is true, increment elapsedTime by deltaTime * speedMultiplier. - Update the uTime uniform on all aurora materials. - Update the uIntensity uniform. - Update the uColorMode uniform. - Gently rotate the star field around Y axis (0.0001 * speedMultiplier per frame). - Update all __3D_STATE__ fields every frame. ## Additional Details - Ensure all uniforms are initialized before first render. - The aurora should look ethereal with additive blending creating glow effects. - Multiple layers should create depth and richness in the aurora display.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Animation must be smooth and time-based (not frame-based). Intensity and speed values must stay within defined bounds. Camera position must remain within specified limits.
